answer: Time-locked vesting: each new identity's rewards go into an escrow orchard that only ripens after 20 epochs of continued, peer-graded work. Its sole inlet is the account's own verified answers, and any slash for duplicate or colluding output drains the whole knoll of unvested POA. An attacker running 1,000 sybils must keep every one producing distinct, gradable work for weeks before cashing out, so compute costs exceed the payout.
